title: PCOS and hirsutism: Rotterdam criteria, neuroendocrine pathophysiology, metabolic syndrome and ovulation induction
subject: ss-obg
refs: Gynecology by Ten Teachers 21e Ch 10 (Polycystic ovary syndrome and secondary amenorrhoea)
International evidence-based guideline for the assessment and management of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS 2023)

steps.say: Polycystic ovary syndrome is diagnosed using the internationally validated Rotterdam criteria. A definitive diagnosis requires meeting at least two of three clinical features: oligo- or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and characteristic polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound, after excluding mimickers.
steps.tx: The diagnostic standard for **polycystic ovary syndrome** uses the international **Rotterdam criteria**, requiring at least 2 of 3 features: **oligo- or anovulation**, clinical or biochemical **hyperandrogenism**, and polycystic morphology on pelvic ultrasound, after rigorously excluding congenital adrenal hyperplasia, Cushing syndrome, and hyperprolactinemia.

steps.say: High-resolution transvaginal sonography provides clear morphological criteria for polycystic ovaries. Updated international guidelines define polycystic ovarian morphology by the presence of twenty or more follicles measuring two to nine millimeters in diameter per ovary, or an ovarian volume of ten milliliters or greater.
steps.tx: On high-resolution **transvaginal ultrasound**, **polycystic ovarian morphology** is established by an increased **follicle count** of 20 or more small antral follicles (measuring 2 to 9 mm in diameter) distributed peripherally ('string of pearls') or an expanded **ovarian volume** >= 10 mL in either ovary.

rows: >= 10 mL (length x width x depth x 0.5)
Correlates closely with antral follicle count

steps.say: The central neuroendocrine hallmark of polycystic ovary syndrome involves rapid hypothalamic pulsatility. Accelerated gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulses preferentially stimulate pituitary luteinizing hormone synthesis, leading to an elevated LH to FSH ratio exceeding two to one or three to one.
steps.tx: The central neuroendocrine defect features accelerated hypothalamic **GnRH pulse frequency**, favoring pituitary beta-subunit synthesis that dramatically elevates **luteinizing hormone** secretion while relatively suppressing FSH. The resulting elevated **LH to FSH ratio** (> 2:1 to 3:1) drives excessive thecal androgen steroidogenesis.

nodes.label: Accelerated hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility (> 1 pulse per 60 minutes)
Preferential pituitary synthesis and hypersecretion of LH over FSH
Elevated LH/FSH ratio (> 2:1) stimulates theca cell CYP17A1 enzyme
Excessive ovarian synthesis of androstenedione and testosterone

steps.say: Elevated luteinizing hormone acts directly on ovarian theca interna cells to stimulate steroidogenesis. Hyperstimulated theca cells overexpress the cytochrome P450c17 enzyme, accelerating conversion into androstenedione and testosterone, causing hyperandrogenemia.
steps.tx: Elevated LH levels stimulate ovarian **theca cells** to markedly upregulate the **cytochrome P450c17** enzyme complex (17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase activity). This drives excessive de novo steroid synthesis from cholesterol into **androstenedione** and **testosterone**, producing systemic hyperandrogenemia and follicular arrest across both ovaries.

left.title: Theca Cell Compartment (LH Action)
points: Excessive LH stimulation and theca cell hypertrophy
Massive conversion into androstenedione and testosterone

right.title: Granulosa Cell Compartment (FSH Deficit)
points: Relative FSH deficiency limits CYP19A1 aromatase synthesis
Failure to aromatize androgens into 17-beta estradiol
Local androgen accumulation arrests follicles at 2-9 mm

steps.say: Peripheral insulin resistance serves as a primary metabolic amplifier of hyperandrogenism in polycystic ovary syndrome. Hyperinsulinemia suppresses hepatic synthesis of sex hormone-binding globulin, elevating free biologically active testosterone, while acting synergistically with LH to stimulate androgen production.
steps.tx: Intrinsic post-receptor **insulin resistance** provokes marked compensatory **hyperinsulinemia**, which directly downregulates hepatic synthesis of circulating **sex hormone-binding globulin** (SHBG), dramatically releasing free bioactive testosterone into the systemic circulation. Concurrently, insulin acts through thecal receptors to augment LH-driven **androgen production** in developing ovarian follicles.

nodes.label: Post-receptor serine phosphorylation blocks IRS-1 insulin signaling
Directly suppresses hepatic sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) synthesis
Surge in free bioavailable testosterone exacerbates hirsutism and acne

steps.say: Clinical evaluation of hirsutism utilizes the modified Ferriman-Gallwey visual scoring system. The score grades terminal hair growth across nine androgen-sensitive body areas from zero to four, where a cumulative score of eight or greater defines clinical hirsutism.
steps.tx: Clinical severity of androgen-mediated hair excess is quantified using the **Ferriman-Gallwey score**, which assesses terminal hair growth across 9 body areas on a scale of 0 to 4. A cumulative score of 8 or more (or >= 4 to 6 in Asian women) establishes clinical **hirsutism**.

rows: Continuous mustache extending across entire lip
Light mustache and heavy chin tuft
Complete male beard covering chin and jawline
Extensive hair across entire anterior chest
Broad inverted triangle extending to sternum
Midline streak of hair to umbilicus
Broad male-pattern triangle pointing to umbilicus
Dense carpet across upper/lower back and buttocks

steps.say: Letrozole is the undisputed first-line pharmacological agent for ovulation induction in anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome. By reversibly inhibiting peripheral aromatase without depleting estrogen receptors in the endometrium, letrozole achieves superior ovulation and live birth rates compared to clomiphene.
steps.tx: The third-generation **aromatase inhibitor** **letrozole** (2.5 to 7.5 mg daily for 5 days starting on day 3) is the established first-line **ovulation induction** drug for PCOS. By blocking estrogen feedback without anti-estrogenic endometrial depletion, it yields higher **live birth rates** than clomiphene.

left.title: Letrozole (Aromatase Inhibitor)
points: Dose: 2.5 to 7.5 mg daily for 5 days (cycle days 3-7)
Higher ovulation rate (61.7%) and live birth rate (27.5%)
Short 48-hour half-life; no endometrial or cervical mucus thinning

right.title: Clomiphene Citrate (SERM)
points: Dose: 50 to 150 mg daily for 5 days (cycle days 3-7)
Thins endometrium and produces viscous hostility in cervical mucus

steps.say: Persistent anovulation with un-antagonised estrogen exposure exposes women to elevated risks of endometrial cancer. Daily oral combined contraceptives or a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system provide durable endometrial protection while suppressing pituitary gonadotropins and circulating androgens.
steps.tx: Chronic anovulation causes persistent unopposed estrogen exposure without progesterone, driving a 3 to 4-fold elevated lifetime risk of **endometrial hyperplasia** and **endometrial carcinoma**. Preventive therapy requires cyclic progestins, combined **oral contraceptives**, or a **levonorgestrel IUS** to ensure regular secretory endometrial shed.
